text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Catholic Church on Sunday implored political parties to denounce violence in the run-up to elections to be held on November 18. The church said in a pastoral letter that it was worried about the tense political mood ahead of the elections.

- Two opposition leaders -- Akashambatwa Mbikusita-Lewanika of the newly formed Agenda for Zambia, and Humphrey Mulemba of the National Party -- on Sunday filed their nomination papers for presidential elections scheduled for November 18. Another opposition leader Chama Chakomboka of Movement for Democratic Process was unable to file his papers because he did not have the money to pay the nomination fee.

- The Zambian Democratic Congress said it may boycott general elections set for November 18 if the government does not address its concerns over the rules to govern elections. Seven other opposition parties have said they would boycott the elections.

- The state-run Zambia National Broadcasting Corp has suspended its controller of television for airing an advertisement in which former president Kenneth Kaunda announced that his party would boycott elections set for November 18.
